title: Refine HackJudge's new visual world
question: Keep Semester Lines, choose a new challenger, or steer the next round.

options.label: Semester Lines
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail maps, enamel signage, and live service diagrams
options.thesis: Events are clear routes through a semester, with scoring, appreciation, and voting as distinct but connected lines.
options.viewport: A live semester diagram connects the focal event to upcoming and past events while the active route opens into its mode-specific action.
options.risk: Lifecycle navigation is exceptionally clear, but projects need strong story panels so they never feel like anonymous stations.
options.case: Still the strongest platform model: high professional clarity, with project storytelling added to earn student delight.

options.label: The Build Sheet
options.lineage: Product teardown manuals, exploded assembly drawings, and engineering review packets
options.thesis: Every project is an engineered object under review, with evidence, decisions, and outcomes annotated directly onto the work.
options.viewport: One featured project or event sits as a large exploded composition, surrounded by its people, criteria, live state, and next action; the system reads like a beautifully edited review packet.
options.risk: Excellent evidence clarity and engineer credibility, but it must celebrate finished work rather than making every student project feel unfinished.
options.case: Wins on professional product clarity; student gratification depends on using annotation as recognition, not inspection theater.

options.label: Signal Horizon
options.lineage: Theater cycloramas, lighting cue sheets, and controlled dawn transitions
options.thesis: An event visibly changes the atmosphere of the whole product as it moves from anticipation to live participation to release.
options.viewport: The focal event lives on a wide horizon whose light phase communicates upcoming, live, closed, or released; precise controls and project stories sit low and clear in the frame.
options.risk: Strong emotional reward and lifecycle memory, but color-rich fields require disciplined contrast and non-color state labels in dense screens.
options.case: Wins on student emotion while retaining clear named states; trails Semester Lines on complex admin navigation.

options.label: Command Elbows
options.lineage: Flat starship wall panels and pill-cornered command banks
options.thesis: HackJudge becomes a lively shared command surface where each event mode is a color bank and the important action is physically obvious.
options.viewport: Thick elbow frames organize one focal event, a ranked bank of projects, and a single bright action segment without relying on cards or page chrome.
options.risk: Highly gratifying and technical, but the sci-fi association can feel costume-like unless the geometry remains restrained and semantic.
options.case: Wins on playful engineer identification; trails both Semester Lines and Build Sheet on neutral professional longevity.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished contemporary SaaS event platform, executed impeccably and without a governing metaphor.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar hero, event cards, project grid, and straightforward application navigation.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but unlikely to give HackJudge a distinctive identity students or judges remember.
